<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown index --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown index [OPTIONS] <PATHS>...
```

## Arguments

`<PATHS>...`
: The drives or folders to index, each as its own root. Roots can't be nested: index each drive or top-level folder once.

## Options

`--cross-filesystems`
: Also descend into other filesystems mounted below PATH.

`--allow-empty`
: Record PATH even if it's now empty although it held files (normally refused: an empty mount point usually means the drive is unplugged).

`--method <METHOD>` {preview}
: How to find what's there: auto (the drive's change log if it's intact, else NTFS's file table where the device can be read, else a walk; and a walk every so often), walk (every folder), journal or table (that way or fail, saying why). Default: `auto`. One of `auto`, `walk`, `journal`, `table`.

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

A drive that is suddenly empty although its last scan held files (usually an unplugged drive's leftover mount point) is refused and nothing is recorded; pass `--allow-empty` if it really was emptied. Symbolic links are not followed. When a daemon is running, the scan is handed to it and it hashes the new files next. With `--method auto`, a rescan reads the drive's change log where there is one (the USN journal of NTFS drives on Windows, the change history of APFS and HFS+ drives on macOS), or NTFS's file table (on Windows as administrator, on Linux for ntfs-3g mounts whose device your account can read), and walks every folder whenever either can't vouch for every file, and anyway every tenth scan or after 30 days (Settings > Scanning). Linux keeps no change log for drives. Each drive's line says how it was scanned and, for a walk, why. `--method journal` or `table` stops with the reason instead of walking.

## Examples

```sh
backdown index /media/old-drive /media/archive
# a NAS share with other file systems mounted inside it
backdown index /mnt/nas --cross-filesystems
# Windows
backdown index E:\ F:\Archive
```
